availability.note: CarExpert 2027 Plus Dark (2.0L, electric) variant page: 'released to the Australian market on 5th June 2026' with a price; CarsGuide 2027 XC90 price page lists 'Plus T8 Dark Phev $120,990' as one of two T8 grades (Plus T8 Dark, Ultra T8 Dark) beside the B5 mild hybrids; CarExpert 2027 range page shows the same two 340kW PHEV grades. volvocars.com/au configurator returned 403, so no manufacturer configurator check

listPrice.note: 'prices starting at $120,990' before on-road costs (CarExpert MY27 variant page; Sydney drive-away $129,157 excludes CTP and dealer delivery). CarsGuide 2027 MSRP $120,990 (https://www.carsguide.com.au/volvo/xc90/price/2027). Unchanged from held. Chasing Cars (22 Sep 2026, https://www.chasingcars.com.au/news/future-cars/a-200km-plug-in-hybrid-2027-volvo-xc60-xc90-phevs-more-than-double-their-electric-range/) quotes the XC90 T8 'from $114,222 before on-roads', unexplained and not adopted (it also mis-states the XC60 by $307 against Volvo's list); Volvo's own price list unreachable (403)

batteryKwh.note: ADAC 'Batteriekapazität' 18,8 kWh brutto, 14,7 kWh netto; CarExpert AU page gives 'Maximum battery kilowatt hour: 18.8 kWh' (gross), same pack. Same net on the Euro 6e-bis listing (https://www.adac.de/rund-ums-fahrzeug/autokatalog/marken-modelle/volvo/xc90/2generation-facelift-2/350415/)

rangeKm.note: European WLTP electric range 71 km (city 89 km) for the T8 Plus Dark on 275/40R21, 07/25-03/26 certification, the listing whose label matches the AU car's older-utility-factor 1.8 L/100km best. AU car rides on 20-inch (275/45 R20). Euro 6e-bis listing (ab 03/26) gives 70 km. CarExpert AU 77 km (CarsGuide review: 'official electric driving range according to Volvo is 77km') is higher than WLTP and rejected by the direction test (NEDC). Held 69 km not re-sourced

consumptionKwhPer100km.note: batteryKwh / rangeKm x 100 = 14.7 / 71 x 100 = 20.7. ADAC WLTP 'Stromverbrauch' 12.8 kWh/100km is utility-factor weighted, not used

combinedRangeKm.note: 71 km WLTP electric + 71 L tank (CarExpert 'Capacity: 71 L'; ADAC 71,0 l) / 7.8 L/100km x 100 = 71 + 910.3 = 981

fuelConsumptionL100km.note: ADAC 'Verbrauch kombiniert (WLTP) PHEV (Batterie leer)' 7,8 l/100 km (CO2 175 g/km battery empty), same basis as mazda-cx-80-phev and kia-sorento-phev (ADAC battery-empty, pre-6e-bis listing). Euro 6e-bis listing (ab 03/26, Plus Bright) gives 7.2. Held 7.7 was a carsales real-world figure. Now sits below volvo-xc60-phev's judged 8.4, which has no WLTP source; the lighter XC60 is the one likely high

isFuelEfficientForLct.note: AU combined-cycle label 'Combined: 1.8 L/100km', at or below 3.5

isGreenForVicDuty.note: SRO green car = passenger car with combined CO2 of 120 g/km or less; CarExpert 'CO2 level - g/km combined: 40 g/km'

bootLitresSeatsUp.note: 'Rear seat up; to lower window: 262 L' (all three rows up, to the belt line); ADAC 'normal' 262 L. Euro 6e-bis Plus Bright lists 244 L, not the AU car

bootLitresSeatsDown.note: ADAC 'dachhoch' (to the roof) with rear seats folded 1816 L; CarExpert 'Rear seat down: 1,816 L'. To-the-roof, matching the folded basis on 7-seat siblings kia-sorento-phev (1988) and mazda-cx-80-phev (1971); ADAC's window-height folded figure is 640 L, which the cargo-cover convention would strictly prefer

towKg.note: 'Gross trailer weight braked: 2,400 kg' (unbraked 750); ADAC 2400 kg (12%). Volvo AU tech sheet unreachable (403)

warrantyYears.note: '60 month, unlimited km warranty', unconditional; battery 96 months/160,000 km

insuranceAnnual.note: Held value kept (list unchanged at $120,990). Anchors: lexus-rx-phev-450h-plus-sports-luxury ($123,650, 2850), volvo-ex90-plus-single-motor ($106,990, 2700), land-rover-defender-phev SE ($131,100, 3000); sits slightly under the Lexus at a slightly lower price

depreciationCurve.note: Owner convention: one Volvo curve, matching volvo-ex90. Evidence for a steep curve: luxury PHEV without the FBT exemption since Apr 2025, and a long-range XC90 T8 with more than double the electric range (164 km WLTP) due Q2 2027 (Chasing Cars, 22 Sep 2026) orphans this 18.8 kWh car. Held curve was [1,0.68,..0.36]/[1,0.66,..0.34]
